newsitem.title: FRANCE: France ready to guarantee Israel border accord.
newsitem.headline: France ready to guarantee Israel border accord.

text.p: French Defence Minister Charles Millon said on Thursday that France was ready to act alongside other nations including the United States as a guarantor to a possible accord on Israel's borders with Lebanon and Syria.

"France has long had friendly relations with Israel and with Arab countries and would like to put these friendships at the disposal of all so that the peace process can be pursued," Millon, on a visit to Israel, told Europe-1 radio in an interview.
He said Israelis wanted their border with Lebanon and Syria to be made safe, "so that it becomes a border of peace".

"France is ready to participate in a global Lebanese-Syrian accord with of course Israel, but with other countries too including the United States and France as guarantors, as witnesses so that the principle of land for peace...can be enacted with Syria and Lebanon as it was with other Middle East countries," Millon said.

Asked whether France was ready to send troops to replace Israeli forces in security zones, Millon answered: "France is in favour of a global accord. France has never shirked its responsibilities when an international action is at stake."

Millon's visit is a sign of warming relations between the two countries. Franco-Israeli ties were cool after Paris slapped an arms embargo on Israel following the 1967 Arab-Israeli war. Links were re-initiated four years ago by then defence minister Francois Leotard.
"Even if there have been high and low points in our relations, all friendships are made of highs and lows. Today France reaffirms its friendship with Israel and vice-versa," Millon said.

But he said France, despite Israeli pressure to boost relations, was cautious on defence and aerospace cooperation with Israel as with other countries of the region. "We want to take part in a peace process, it is out of the question that we take part in an arms race."

Millon's visit is one of several French ministerial visits recently announced by Prime Minister Alain Juppe, who is seeking to mend bridges with French Jews ahead of France's 1988 general election and after a controversial Middle East tour by President Jacques Chirac in October.
